extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors at Nature Communications and other journal stakeholders interested in implementing transparent peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy criteria for implementing transparent peer review at a research journal: what to publish, who must consent, how anonymity is handled, and metrics to track uptake and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of reviewer reports and author rebuttals (author opt-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish reviewer reports and author rebuttal letters for papers submitted from January 2016 onwards, but only if authors agree to this upon acceptance of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked at acceptance to opt in to having the peer review files published; authors have the option to opt out of the scheme. The stated intention is to open up the peer review process and provide information on the expert reports that led to the editorial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer consent to potential publication (condition of reviewing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas authors do have the option to opt out of the scheme, this is not the case for reviewers, who have to agree to the potential publication of their reviewer reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must agree to the possibility that their reports may be published as part of the review file; a small number of reviewers have declined to review under this circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity preserved by default
rubrics_metrics.description: The anonymity of our reviewers is maintained, unless they sign their reports to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may choose to sign reports (thereby revealing their identity); otherwise anonymity is retained in published files. Privacy and identifiability concerns (especially in small research areas) are acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and content of published peer review files
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review files published contain reviewer reports and author rebuttal letters (the peer review history of the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published files serve as background on the merits of a study and inform about the discussion between authors and reviewers; files may be included as supplementary information (e.g., a 'peer review file' PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and report author opt-in rates by research area
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate at which authors are opting in to publication of peer review files is crucial to the success of transparent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Communications tracked opt-in for 787 qualifying papers and reported an average opt-in across the journal of about 60%, with variation by research field. Reporting uptake by area can reveal where transparent review is more or less accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reader engagement and feedback on published review files
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess reader interaction with the peer review files, such as downloads and feedback, to evaluate the impact of transparent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With more time it may be possible to study number of downloads in detail; anecdotal instances include authors promoting positive reviewer comments and readers commenting on peer review discussions, showcasing potential for appreciation and constructive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide support measures for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Take steps to support reviewers in the transparent peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other steps to support reviewers are described in a separate editorial (referenced). Support can help reduce friction and encourage participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider privacy and identifiability risks, especially in small fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful that publishing reviewer reports can increase the risk of reviewers being identified in small research areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy recognizes cases where reviewers objected because they feared it would be easy to deduce their identity; allowing reviewers to decline to review is an accommodation for such concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make transparent peer review a permanent, evaluated feature
rubrics_metrics.description: If uptake and benefits are encouraging, incorporate transparent peer review as a permanent journal feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Communications moved from a trial to making the scheme a permanent feature, with the expectation that more authors and readers will appreciate the benefits over time; continued monitoring of uptake and impacts is implied.
